 Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo drives against Kevin Huerter #27 and Cade Cunningham of the Detroit Pistons during the third quarter of the game at Kaseya Center on November 14, 2026 in Miami, Florida. (Megan Briggs/Getty Images) 
 By Ira Winderman | iwinderman@sunsentinel.com | South Florida Sun Sentinel PUBLISHED: November 14, 2026 at 10:46 PM EST | UPDATED: November 14, 2026 at 11:10 PM EST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... MIAMI – Observations and other notes of interest from Saturday night’s 137-117 victory over the Detroit Pistons:
 – The metronome at the start of this one was this:
 – Whistle. Whistle. Whistle. Whistle.
 – Foul. Foul. Foul. Foul.
 – Continuity was at a minimum.
 – In other words, it would come down more to the players than the plays.
 – Individual will, if you will.
 – Leaving the Heat even more appreciative that Giannis Antetokounmpo is on their side .
 – Continually seizing moments when the Heat needed to be seized, Antetokounmpo again displayed the versatility that makes him unique among big men.
 – Doing it on both ends.
 – On one hand, that required another night of heavy lifting for the Heat’s prized offseason acquisition on the second night of a back-to-back set that opened with him going for 37 points Friday night against the Cavaliers .
 – On the other hand, it is exactly why he was brought to the Heat at such an extensive trade cost.
 – When the Heat were down at the start of the season, Antetokounmpo vowed he and his team would be better.
 – With the Heat now over .500 for the first time this season, Antetokounmpo and his team have been better.
 – With Klay Thompson (ankle) back after sitting out Friday night, but Pelle Larsson (illness) still out, Erik Spoelstra again had Myron Gardner in the Heat starting lineup, along with Antetokounmpo, Bam Adebayo, Davion Mitchell and Thompson.
 – Gardner was his typical feisty self, first jawing at Duncan Robinson and later called for a double technical foul in the second period along with the Pistons’ Ron Holland.
 – The Pistons opened with a lineup of  John Collins, Duncan Robinson, Cade Cunningham, Ausar Thompson and Daniss Jenkins.
 – Ryan Conwell was first off the Heat bench.
 – Followed by Bobby Portis Jr.
 – And then Andrew Wiggins.
 – With Simone Fontecchio entering at the start of the second quarter.
 – Then, with the Heat dealing with foul trouble, Nikola Jovic also got a shot.
 – Spoelstra reiterated pregame that when teammates run with Mitchell, good things happen.
 – “We want to have guys run with him,” Spoelstra said. “He’s fast with the ball and he’s unselfish.He wants to set guys up, but it takes our guys sacrificing and running.”
 – In the injury absence of sidelined Jalen Duren, Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff said it only has been natural to turn to the 3-point shooting of former Heat guard Duncan Robinson.
 – “We wanted to create more movement, and he’s a natural mover,” Bickerstaff said “He does a great job. We want him to hunt threes, and that’s been our message to him. And, you know, there’s 10 of them a night.We’d like to see him get 12 to 15 of them a night.But, again, he’s accepted that role because he knows we need it.”
 – Robinson then was lost to injury in the second period.
 – Spoelstra was effusive pregame in his praise for Pistons guard Cade Cunningham.
 – “You can see how he processes defenses and he can see things before they happen,” Spoelstra said. “He has the size. He can deliver the ball. He’s not selfish. But he also can score. He can really put some pressure on your defense.”

 – It was the Heat’s NBA-best 32nd consecutive game scoring at least 100 points at home.
 – The game closed the Heat’s third of the Heat’s 13 back-to-back sets of the season, having defeated the visiting Cavaliers on Friday night.
 – The Heat entered 0-2 this season on the second nights of such pairings.
 – It was the 45th time in franchise history the Heat played consecutive home games, previously having won both 14 times, split 20 times and lost both 10 times.
 – Meanwhile, the Heat’s Vlad Goldin was on assignment with the Heat’s G League affiliate, the Sioux Falls Skyforce.
 – Because of the impact of Friday’s FAA ground stop, the Heat’s G League team had to van 5 1/2 hours from Chicago to Cleveland for that Saturday game.
 – Goldin, the former FAU center on a Heat two-way contract, closed that game with 31 points on 14-of-18 shooting, eight rebounds.
 – Shakira was among the faces in the crowd.
